records.source: וְאַבְרָהָ֣ם זָקֵ֔ן בָּ֖א בַּיָּמִ֑ים וַֽיהוָ֛ה בֵּרַ֥ךְ אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֖ם בַּכֹּֽל׃
records.gloss: And Abraham [was] old, gone into the days; and YHWH had blessed Abraham in everything.
pieces: Abraham had grown old; he was far on in years, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had given him blessing in every part of his life.

L.1: Now Abraham was old, advanced in days, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had blessed Abraham in everything.

R.1: By now Abraham was a very old man. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had blessed him in all he had and all he did.

decisions.choice: advanced in days: very old
decisions.reason: The phrase "come into the days" means well on in years (18:11). It explains why Abraham now settles his son's marriage: he wants to see it done while he lives.

decisions.choice: blessed Abraham in everything: the promise of 12:2 kept
decisions.reason: God had promised "I will bless you" (12:2). The chapter opens by saying the promise has come true in every part of Abraham's life; the servant repeats it to Laban (verse 35).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַבְרָהָ֗ם אֶל־עַבְדּוֹ֙ זְקַ֣ן בֵּית֔וֹ הַמֹּשֵׁ֖ל בְּכָל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֑וֹ שִֽׂים־נָ֥א יָדְךָ֖ תַּ֥חַת יְרֵכִֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Abraham to his servant, [the] elder of his house, the [one] ruling over all that [was] to him, put, please, your hand under my thigh,
pieces: Abraham said to the servant who was the elder of his household and steward of all he possessed, "Place your hand under my thigh,

L.2: And Abraham said to his slave, the eldest of his household, who ruled over all that he had, "Please put your hand under my thigh,

R.2: Abraham called the servant who had been in his household longest, the one in charge of everything he owned. Abraham said to him, "Put your hand under my thigh and make me a promise.

decisions.choice: his slave, the eldest of his household: the chief steward
decisions.reason: The word eved is used of a slave owned by his master. "The eldest of his household" may mean the oldest or, more likely, the most senior, the steward who ran Abraham's estate. He is not named; some identify him with Eliezer of Damascus (15:2), but the chapter never says so.

decisions.choice: put your hand under my thigh: a solemn way of taking an oath
decisions.reason: Jacob asks Joseph for the same gesture (47:29). The "thigh" is near the organs of procreation, so the oath is probably sworn by the life and descendants of the one who asks it, the very matter at stake here. It made the promise binding and sacred.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that he was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: and make me a promise
decisions.reason: Readable says at once what the gesture is for; the oath itself follows in verse 3.

records.source: וְאַשְׁבִּ֣יעֲךָ֔ בַּֽיהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וֵֽאלֹהֵ֖י הָאָ֑רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־תִקַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ לִבְנִ֔י מִבְּנוֹת֙ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י יוֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: and I will make you swear by YHWH, [the] God of the heavens and [the] God of the earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from [the] daughters of the Canaanite[s] among whom I [am] dwelling,
pieces: so that I can bind you by an oath in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, God of heaven and God of earth. You must not get a wife for my son from the Canaanite women of the land where I am living.

L.3: and I will make you swear by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the heavens and the God of the earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell,

R.3: Swear to me by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God who rules heaven and earth, that you will not choose a wife for my son from the Canaanite women who live around me.

decisions.choice: the God of the heavens and the God of the earth: Lord of all places
decisions.reason: Abraham swears his slave by the God who rules everywhere, not a local god of Canaan. The same God can guide the slave on a long journey to a foreign land (verse 7).

decisions.choice: not from the daughters of the Canaanites: keeping the promised line apart
decisions.reason: Marriage joined families and their gods. Abraham will not have Isaac, the heir of the promise, married into the peoples of Canaan, whose ways the LORD would judge (15:16). Isaac and Rebekah later grieve over Esau's Canaanite wives (26:34-35; 27:46; 28:1).

records.source: כִּ֧י אֶל־אַרְצִ֛י וְאֶל־מוֹלַדְתִּ֖י תֵּלֵ֑ךְ וְלָקַחְתָּ֥ אִשָּׁ֖ה לִבְנִ֥י לְיִצְחָֽק׃
records.gloss: but to my land and to my kindred you will go, and you will take a wife for my son, for Isaac.
pieces: Instead, travel to the land I come from, to my own people, and find a wife there for my son Isaac."

L.4: but you will go to my land and to my kindred, and take a wife for my son, for Isaac."

R.4: Go back to the land I came from, to my relatives, and find a wife there for my son Isaac."

decisions.choice: my land and my kindred: Abraham's relatives in Aram
decisions.reason: Abraham's brother Nahor and his family stayed in upper Mesopotamia (11:29-31; 22:20-23). Marriage within the wider family was the custom; Jacob too finds his wives there (28:2).

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ הָעֶ֔בֶד אוּלַי֙ לֹא־תֹאבֶ֣ה הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה לָלֶ֥כֶת אַחֲרַ֖י אֶל־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את הֶֽהָשֵׁ֤ב אָשִׁיב֙ אֶת־בִּנְךָ֔ אֶל־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־יָצָ֥אתָ מִשָּֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And said to him the servant, perhaps not will be willing the woman to go after me to this land; must I indeed take back your son to the land from which you came out?
pieces: The servant asked him, "Suppose the woman refuses to follow me here. Am I then to take your son back to the land you came out of?"

L.5: And the slave said to him, "Perhaps the woman will not be willing to follow me to this land. Must I then take your son back to the land you came from?"

R.5: The servant asked, "But the woman might not want to leave home and come here with me. Then should I take your son to the land you came from?"

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו אַבְרָהָ֑ם הִשָּׁ֣מֶר לְךָ֔ פֶּן־תָּשִׁ֥יב אֶת־בְּנִ֖י שָֽׁמָּה׃
records.gloss: And said to him Abraham, take heed to yourself, lest you take back my son there.
pieces: "On no account take my son back there," Abraham answered.

L.6: And Abraham said to him, "Take care that you do not take my son back there.

R.6: Abraham answered, "No! Never take my son back there.

decisions.choice: do not take my son back there: Isaac must stay in the promised land
decisions.reason: God called Abraham out of that land and promised him this one (12:1, 7). For Isaac to go back would be to turn away from the promise. The point is said twice (verse 8).

records.source: יְהוָ֣ה׀אֱלֹהֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם אֲשֶׁ֨ר לְקָחַ֜נִי מִבֵּ֣ית אָבִי֮ וּמֵאֶ֣רֶץ מֽוֹלַדְתִּי֒ וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּר־לִ֜י וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר נִֽשְׁבַּֽע־לִי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לְזַ֨רְעֲךָ֔ אֶתֵּ֖ן אֶת־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את ה֗וּא יִשְׁלַ֤ח מַלְאָכוֹ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ וְלָקַחְתָּ֥ אִשָּׁ֛ה לִבְנִ֖י מִשָּֽׁם׃
records.gloss: YHWH, [the] God of the heavens, who took me from [the] house of my father and from [the] land of my kindred, and who spoke to me and who swore to me, saying, to your offspring I will give this land, he will send his angel before you, and you will take a wife for my son from there.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of heaven, took me from my father's family and the land of my birth. He spoke to me and swore to me, 'I will give this land to your descendants.' He will send {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angel ahead of you, and you will find a wife there for my son.

L.7: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the heavens, who took me from my father's house and from the land of my kindred, and who spoke to me and swore to me, saying, 'To your offspring I will give this land,' {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angel before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there.

R.7: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of heaven, brought me out of my father's home and my homeland. He made a promise to me with an oath. He said, 'I will give this land to your descendants.' He will send {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angel to go ahead of you. And you will find a wife there for my son.

decisions.choice: who took me from my father's house: the call of 12:1
decisions.reason: Abraham recalls how God called him away from his country, his kindred and his father's house (12:1). The God who led him then will lead his slave now.

decisions.choice: who swore to me: the oath of 22:16-18
decisions.reason: God's promise of the land to Abraham's offspring (12:7; 13:15) was sworn with an oath after Abraham offered Isaac (22:16-18). These are the last words of Abraham recorded in Genesis.

decisions.choice: his angel: God's messenger, who guides
decisions.reason: The word mal'akh means a messenger. Abraham trusts that God will send his angel to go before the slave and guide him, as the angel later guided Israel (Exodus 23:20). No angel appears in the story, yet the slave is guided at every step.

decisions.choice: he, his (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: Pronouns for God take the deity pronoun setting; at the start of a sentence they are capitalized in any case.

decisions.choice: offspring (L), descendants (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word (zera) is "seed"; as in earlier chapters, Literal says "offspring" and Balanced and Readable say "descendants".

records.source: וְאִם־לֹ֨א תֹאבֶ֤ה הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ לָלֶ֣כֶת אַחֲרֶ֔יךָ וְנִקִּ֕יתָ מִשְּׁבֻעָתִ֖י זֹ֑את רַ֣ק אֶת־בְּנִ֔י לֹ֥א תָשֵׁ֖ב שָֽׁמָּה׃
records.gloss: And if not will be willing the woman to go after you, then you will be free from this my oath; only my son, not you must take back there.
pieces: If the woman refuses to come, this oath will no longer bind you. Only, my son must never be taken back there."

L.8: And if the woman is not willing to follow you, then you will be free from this oath of mine. Only you must not take my son back there."

R.8: If the woman will not come with you, then you do not have to keep this promise to me. But you must never take my son back there."

decisions.choice: free from my oath: released from its curse
decisions.reason: An oath carried a curse on the one who broke it. If the woman refuses, the slave has not failed his oath and no curse falls on him (compare verse 41, which uses a stronger word).

records.source: וַיָּ֤שֶׂם הָעֶ֨בֶד֙ אֶת־יָד֔וֹ תַּ֛חַת יֶ֥רֶךְ אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֑יו וַיִּשָּׁ֣בַֽע ל֔וֹ עַל־הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And put the servant his hand under [the] thigh of Abraham his master and swore to him concerning this matter.
pieces: So the servant placed his hand under the thigh of his master Abraham and took the oath he asked for.

L.9: So the slave put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master and swore to him concerning this matter.

R.9: So the servant put his hand under Abraham's thigh and promised to do what his master asked.

decisions.choice: his master: literally "his masters"
decisions.reason: The word for master (adon) is often plural in form when it refers to one person, to show respect. It is used throughout the chapter of Abraham, one man.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֣ח הָ֠עֶבֶד עֲשָׂרָ֨ה גְמַלִּ֜ים מִגְּמַלֵּ֤י אֲדֹנָיו֙ וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ וְכָל־ט֥וּב אֲדֹנָ֖יו בְּיָד֑וֹ וַיָּ֗קָם וַיֵּ֛לֶךְ אֶל־אֲרַ֥ם נַֽהֲרַ֖יִם אֶל־עִ֥יר נָחֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: And took the servant ten camels from [the] camels of his master and went; and every good thing of his master [was] in his hand; and he arose and went to Aram-naharaim, to [the] city of Nahor.
pieces: The servant took ten camels from his master's herd and set off, carrying with him all sorts of fine things from his master. He made the journey to Aram-naharaim, to the town where Nahor lived.

L.10: And the slave took ten of his master's camels and went, with all kinds of good things from his master in his hand; and he arose and went to Aram-naharaim, to the city of Nahor.

R.10: The servant took ten of Abraham's camels and loaded them with all kinds of valuable gifts from his master. Then he set out on the long trip to northern Mesopotamia, to the town where Abraham's brother Nahor lived.

decisions.choice: Aram-naharaim: "Aram of the two rivers"
decisions.reason: The name means the land of the Arameans between or beside two rivers, the Euphrates and its tributaries, in upper Mesopotamia. Abraham's family had lived at Haran there (11:31; 27:43).

decisions.choice: the city of Nahor: Nahor's town
decisions.reason: This may mean the town where Nahor, Abraham's brother, lived (probably Haran, 27:43), or a town called Nahor; a place of that name is known in the region from ancient records. Either way it is where Abraham's kin lived.

decisions.choice: ten camels and every good thing: a rich man's embassy
decisions.reason: Ten camels were a great show of wealth, and the good things were gifts for the bride and her family (verses 22, 53). They prove to Rebekah's family that Abraham can provide well for her.

decisions.choice: northern Mesopotamia
decisions.reason: Readable gives the region a name a modern reader can place (m1).

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַיַּבְרֵ֧ךְ הַגְּמַלִּ֛ים מִח֥וּץ לָעִ֖יר אֶל־בְּאֵ֣ר הַמָּ֑יִם לְעֵ֣ת עֶ֔רֶב לְעֵ֖ת צֵ֥את הַשֹּׁאֲבֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And he made kneel the camels outside the city by [the] well of water at [the] time of evening, at [the] time of going out of the [women who] draw water.
pieces: He brought the camels to their knees beside the well outside the town at evening, the hour when the women went out for water.

L.11: And he made the camels kneel outside the city by the well of water, at the time of evening, the time when the women go out to draw water.

R.11: When he got there, he made the camels kneel down near the well outside the town. It was evening, the time when the women came out to get water.

decisions.choice: the time when the women go out to draw water
decisions.reason: Fetching water was women's work, done in the cool of the evening (compare 29:9-10; Exodus 2:16). The slave waits where he is sure to meet the young women of the town.

records.source: וַיֹּאמַ֓ר׀יְהוָ֗ה אֱלֹהֵי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֔ם הַקְרֵה־נָ֥א לְפָנַ֖י הַיּ֑וֹם וַעֲשֵׂה־חֶ֕סֶד עִ֖ם אֲדֹנִ֥י אַבְרָהָֽם׃
records.gloss: And he said, YHWH, God of my master Abraham, make happen, please, before me today and do loyalty with my master Abraham.
pieces: Then he prayed: "{{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, God of my master Abraham, let things go well for me today. Show your faithful love to my master Abraham.

L.12: And he said, "{{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, God of my master Abraham, please grant me success today, and show loyalty to my master Abraham.

R.12: Then he prayed, "{{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, God of my master Abraham, please help me find what I am looking for today. Show your kindness to my master Abraham.

decisions.choice: make it happen before me: let me meet the right person
decisions.reason: The verb (qarah, in a causative form) means to make something happen or come one's way. The slave asks God to arrange the meeting he needs.

decisions.choice: loyalty (chesed): faithful kindness
decisions.reason: Chesed is kindness that keeps faith with someone, the love of one bound by promise (19:19). The word runs through the chapter (verses 14, 27, 49): the slave asks God to keep faith with Abraham, and in the end praises him for it.

decisions.choice: the first prayer for guidance in the Bible
decisions.reason: The slave of Abraham prays in his master's name to his master's God. His prayer is answered before he has finished (verse 15).

records.source: הִנֵּ֛ה אָנֹכִ֥י נִצָּ֖ב עַל־עֵ֣ין הַמָּ֑יִם וּבְנוֹת֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י הָעִ֔יר יֹצְאֹ֖ת לִשְׁאֹ֥ב מָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: Here, I [am] standing by [the] spring of water, and [the] daughters of [the] men of the city [are] coming out to draw water.
pieces: Here I stand at the spring, while the young women of the town come out for water.

L.13: Look, I am standing by the spring of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.

R.13: I am standing here by the spring, and the girls from the town are coming out to get water.

decisions.choice: spring and well: the same place
decisions.reason: The narrator calls the water source a well (be'er, verse 11), the slave a spring ('ayin). It was probably a spring with steps leading down to it (verse 16, "she went down").

records.source: וְהָיָ֣ה הַֽנַּעֲרָ֗ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֹמַ֤ר אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ הַטִּי־נָ֤א כַדֵּךְ֙ וְאֶשְׁתֶּ֔ה וְאָמְרָ֣ה שְׁתֵ֔ה וְגַם־גְּמַלֶּ֖יךָ אַשְׁקֶ֑ה אֹתָ֤הּ הֹכַ֨חְתָּ֙ לְעַבְדְּךָ֣ לְיִצְחָ֔ק וּבָ֣הּ אֵדַ֔ע כִּי־עָשִׂ֥יתָ חֶ֖סֶד עִם־אֲדֹנִֽי׃
records.gloss: And let it be [that] the young woman to whom I say, bend down, please, your jar that I may drink, and she says, drink, and also your camels I will give drink, her you have appointed for your servant, for Isaac; and by it I will know that you have done loyalty with my master.
pieces: I will say to one of the girls, 'Please tip your jar so that I can have a drink.' If she answers, 'Drink, and I will water your camels as well,' may she prove to be the girl {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have picked out for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant Isaac. That is how I will know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have kept faith with my master."

L.14: Let it be that the young woman to whom I say, 'Please lower your jar so that I may drink,' and who says, 'Drink, and I will also water your camels,' is the one {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have appointed for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant Isaac. By this I will know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have shown loyalty to my master."

R.14: I will say to one of the girls, 'Please lower your jar and let me have a drink.' If she says, 'Have a drink, and I will give your camels water too,' then let her be the one {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have chosen to be the wife of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant Isaac. Then I will know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been kind to my master."

decisions.choice: I will water your camels too: a sign of character
decisions.reason: A thirsty camel can drink many gallons, and ten camels need a great deal of water drawn by hand. The sign the slave asks for is no mere chance: it would show a young woman who is generous, strong and hard-working, and hospitable to a stranger.

decisions.choice: you have appointed: chosen, decided on
decisions.reason: The verb (yakach, causative) means to decide or settle a matter; here, to choose and assign the woman for Isaac. Isaac is called God's "servant", as one who belongs to him.

decisions.choice: young woman: written without its last letter
decisions.reason: In the five books of Moses the word for young woman (na'arah) is usually written without its final letter, so that it looks like the word for young man (na'ar). It is read as feminine, as the context requires. The meaning is not affected.

decisions.choice: you, your (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: The slave speaks to God, so "you" and "your" take the deity pronoun setting.

records.source: וַֽיְהִי־ה֗וּא טֶרֶם֮ כִּלָּ֣ה לְדַבֵּר֒ וְהִנֵּ֧ה רִבְקָ֣ה יֹצֵ֗את אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֻלְּדָה֙ לִבְתוּאֵ֣ל בֶּן־מִלְכָּ֔ה אֵ֥שֶׁת נָח֖וֹר אֲחִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֑ם וְכַדָּ֖הּ עַל־שִׁכְמָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And it was, he had not yet finished speaking, and there, Rebekah [was] coming out, who had been born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, wife of Nahor, brother of Abraham; and her jar [was] on her shoulder.
pieces: The words were hardly out of his mouth when Rebekah appeared, carrying her jar on her shoulder. Her father was Bethuel, son of Milcah and of Nahor, Abraham's brother.

L.15: And before he had finished speaking, look, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother, with her jar on her shoulder.

R.15: Before he finished praying, Rebekah came out with her water jar on her shoulder. Her father was Bethuel, the son of Milcah and Nahor. Nahor was Abraham's brother.

decisions.choice: before he had finished speaking: an answer already on its way
decisions.reason: The narrator stresses that the prayer is answered at once; the slave says the same (verse 45). Compare Isaiah 65:24.

decisions.choice: Rebekah, granddaughter of Nahor and Milcah
decisions.reason: The reader knows from 22:20-23 that Rebekah belongs to Abraham's family, the very family Abraham named. The slave does not yet know it (verse 23).

records.source: וְהַֽנַּעֲרָ֗ טֹבַ֤ת מַרְאֶה֙ מְאֹ֔ד בְּתוּלָ֕ה וְאִ֖ישׁ לֹ֣א יְדָעָ֑הּ וַתֵּ֣רֶד הָעַ֔יְנָה וַתְּמַלֵּ֥א כַדָּ֖הּ וַתָּֽעַל׃
records.gloss: And the young woman [was] good of appearance exceedingly, a virgin, and a man had not known her; and she went down to the spring and filled her jar and came up.
pieces: The girl was strikingly beautiful and a virgin, untouched by any man. Down to the spring she went, filled her jar, and climbed up again.

L.16: And the young woman was very good-looking, a virgin; no man had known her. And she went down to the spring and filled her jar and came up.

R.16: Rebekah was very beautiful. She was a virgin who had never been with a man. She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and climbed back up.

decisions.choice: a virgin, and no man had known her
decisions.reason: Betulah often means a young woman of marriageable age; the added words make clear she had never had sexual relations. "Know" is used for sexual union (4:1; 19:8). She is a fitting bride for Isaac.

records.source: וַיָּ֥רָץ הָעֶ֖בֶד לִקְרָאתָ֑הּ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הַגְמִיאִ֥ינִי נָ֛א מְעַט־מַ֖יִם מִכַּדֵּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And ran the servant to meet her and said, give me to drink, please, a little water from your jar.
pieces: The servant ran to meet her. "Please," he said, "let me have a sip of water from your jar."

L.17: And the slave ran to meet her and said, "Please give me a little water to drink from your jar."

R.17: The servant ran up to her and said, "Please let me drink a little water from your jar."

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַתֹּ֖אמֶר שְׁתֵ֣ה אֲדֹנִ֑י וַתְּמַהֵ֗ר וַתֹּ֧רֶד כַּדָּ֛הּ עַל־יָדָ֖הּ וַתַּשְׁקֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And she said, drink, my lord; and she hurried and lowered her jar upon her hand and gave him drink.
pieces: "Drink, sir," she said, and at once she let her jar down onto her hands and held it for him to drink.

L.18: And she said, "Drink, my lord," and she quickly lowered her jar onto her hand and gave him a drink.

R.18: "Drink, sir," she said. She quickly lowered the jar from her shoulder and held it so he could drink.

decisions.choice: she hurried: eager and generous
decisions.reason: Rebekah's speed is stressed again and again (verses 18, 20, 28). Like Abraham hurrying to serve his guests (18:6-7), she shows hospitality without being asked twice.

records.source: וַתְּכַ֖ל לְהַשְׁקֹת֑וֹ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר גַּ֤ם לִגְמַלֶּ֨יךָ֙ אֶשְׁאָ֔ב עַ֥ד אִם־כִּלּ֖וּ לִשְׁתֹּֽת׃
records.gloss: And she finished giving him drink and said, also for your camels I will draw water until they have finished drinking.
pieces: When he had drunk enough, she said, "I will fetch water for your camels as well, until they have had all they want."

L.19: When she had finished giving him a drink, she said, "I will draw water for your camels too, until they have finished drinking."

R.19: When he finished drinking, she said, "I will get water for your camels too, until they are not thirsty anymore."

decisions.choice: for your camels too: the sign fulfilled word for word
decisions.reason: Without knowing it, Rebekah offers exactly what the slave had asked God for as a sign (verse 14), and more: she will keep drawing until the camels are satisfied.

records.source: וַתְּמַהֵ֗ר וַתְּעַ֤ר כַּדָּהּ֙ אֶל־הַשֹּׁ֔קֶת וַתָּ֥רָץ ע֛וֹד אֶֽל־הַבְּאֵ֖ר לִשְׁאֹ֑ב וַתִּשְׁאַ֖ב לְכָל־גְּמַלָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And she hurried and emptied her jar into the trough and ran again to the well to draw water, and she drew water for all his camels.
pieces: Without delay she tipped out her jar into the trough and ran back to the well, drawing water again and again until every one of his camels had drunk.

L.20: And she quickly emptied her jar into the trough and ran again to the well to draw water, and she drew for all his camels.

R.20: She quickly emptied her jar into the drinking trough. Then she ran back to the well again and again, until she had brought water for all his camels.

decisions.choice: again and again
decisions.reason: Watering ten camels took many trips; Balanced and Readable make that clear.

records.source: וְהָאִ֥ישׁ מִשְׁתָּאֵ֖ה לָ֑הּ מַחֲרִ֕ישׁ לָדַ֗עַת הַֽהִצְלִ֧יחַ יְהוָ֛ה דַּרְכּ֖וֹ אִם־לֹֽא׃
records.gloss: And the man [was] gazing at her, keeping silent, to know whether had made successful YHWH his journey or not.
pieces: The man stood gazing at her without a word, waiting to see whether {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had blessed his journey with success or not.

L.21: And the man gazed at her in silence, to learn whether {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had made his journey successful or not.

R.21: The man watched her without saying a word. He wanted to know for sure whether {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had made his trip a success.

decisions.choice: gazing in silence: watching closely, holding back
decisions.reason: The first verb (sha'ah, in an unusual form) may mean to gaze intently or to be astonished. The man waits to see whether the sign will be completed before he speaks.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר כִּלּ֤וּ הַגְּמַלִּים֙ לִשְׁתּ֔וֹת וַיִּקַּ֤ח הָאִישׁ֙ נֶ֣זֶם זָהָ֔ב בֶּ֖קַע מִשְׁקָל֑וֹ וּשְׁנֵ֤י צְמִידִים֙ עַל־יָדֶ֔יהָ עֲשָׂרָ֥ה זָהָ֖ב מִשְׁקָלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And it was, when had finished the camels drinking, and took the man a ring of gold, a beka its weight, and two bracelets for her hands, ten [shekels of] gold their weight.
pieces: Once the camels had drunk their fill, the man brought out a gold ring for her nose, {{units:about a fifth of an ounce|a beka}} in weight, and two bracelets of gold for her arms, weighing {{units:about 4 ounces|ten shekels}}.

L.22: And when the camels had finished drinking, the man took a gold ring weighing a beka, and two bracelets for her arms weighing ten [shekels] of gold.

R.22: When the camels were done drinking, the man took out a gold ring for her nose. It weighed {{units:about a fifth of an ounce|a beka}}. He also took out two gold bracelets for her arms. They weighed {{units:about 4 ounces|ten shekels}}.

decisions.choice: a gold ring: a nose ring
decisions.reason: The word nezem can mean a nose ring or an earring. Verse 47 says the slave put it on her nose.

decisions.choice: a beka and ten shekels: weights of gold
decisions.reason: A beka was half a shekel (Exodus 38:26), about 0.2 ounce (5.7 grams); ten shekels were about 4 ounces (115 grams). These were rich gifts, a first sign of Abraham's wealth.

decisions.choice: about a fifth of an ounce, about 4 ounces; with the Measures setting, a beka, ten shekels
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give modern weights by default and the original units as the setting's alternative; Literal keeps the original units.

decisions.choice: nose ring
decisions.reason: Verse 47 shows it was for her nose (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ בַּת־מִ֣י אַ֔תְּ הַגִּ֥ידִי נָ֖א לִ֑י הֲיֵ֧שׁ בֵּית־אָבִ֛יךְ מָק֥וֹם לָ֖נוּ לָלִֽין׃
records.gloss: And he said, daughter of whom [are] you? Tell me, please; is there in [the] house of your father room for us to lodge?
pieces: "Tell me, please, whose daughter you are," he said. "And would your father's household have space for us to stay the night?"

L.23: And he said, "Whose daughter are you? Please tell me. Is there room in your father's house for us to spend the night?"

R.23: He asked her, "Who is your father? Please tell me. Is there room at your father's house for us to stay tonight?"

decisions.choice: room for us to spend the night: asking for hospitality
decisions.reason: There were no inns in such a town; travelers relied on the hospitality of local households (19:2-3). The slave travels with several men (verse 32) and ten camels, so he asks whether there is room.

records.source: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו בַּת־בְּתוּאֵ֖ל אָנֹ֑כִי בֶּן־מִלְכָּ֕ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָלְדָ֖ה לְנָחֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: And she said to him, [the] daughter of Bethuel I [am], [the] son of Milcah whom she bore to Nahor.
pieces: "My father is Bethuel," she told him, "Milcah's son by Nahor."

L.24: And she said to him, "I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor."

R.24: She answered, "My father is Bethuel. His parents are Milcah and Nahor."

records.source: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו גַּם־תֶּ֥בֶן גַּם־מִסְפּ֖וֹא רַ֣ב עִמָּ֑נוּ גַּם־מָק֖וֹם לָלֽוּן׃
records.gloss: And she said to him, both straw and fodder [is] plenty with us, also room to lodge.
pieces: "There is straw and feed in plenty at our place," she went on, "and a place for you to sleep as well."

L.25: And she said to him, "We have plenty of both straw and fodder, and also room to spend the night."

R.25: Then she said, "We have plenty of straw and food for your camels. And we have room for you to spend the night."

decisions.choice: straw and fodder: feed for the camels
decisions.reason: Straw (teven) was chopped stalks of grain; fodder (mispo) was other feed for animals. Rebekah offers more than was asked, as she did at the well.

records.source: וַיִּקֹּ֣ד הָאִ֔ישׁ וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ לַֽיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And bowed the man and bowed down to YHWH.
pieces: The man knelt low and worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.26: And the man bowed his head and worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.26: Then the man bent down low to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: bowed his head and worshiped: two words for bowing
decisions.reason: The first verb (qadad) is to bow the head; the second (hishtachavah) is to bow down to the ground in worship. Together they show deep reverence and thanks.

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֔ם אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־עָזַ֥ב חַסְדּ֛וֹ וַאֲמִתּ֖וֹ מֵעִ֣ם אֲדֹנִ֑י אָנֹכִ֗י בַּדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ נָחַ֣נִי יְהוָ֔ה בֵּ֖ית אֲחֵ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי׃
records.gloss: And he said, blessed [be] YHWH, [the] God of my master Abraham, who has not left his loyalty and his faithfulness from with my master; I, on the way, has led me YHWH [to the] house of [the] brothers of my master.
pieces: "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of my master Abraham, be praised!" he said. "He has not stopped being kind and true to my master. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has guided me on my way straight to the home of my master's relatives."

L.27: And he said, "Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of my master Abraham, who has not withdrawn {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyalty and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithfulness from my master. As for me, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has led me on the way to the house of my master's kinsmen."

R.27: He said, "Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of my master Abraham! He has kept {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loving promises to my master. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has led me straight to the house of my master's relatives."

decisions.choice: loyalty and faithfulness (chesed ve'emet): love that keeps its promises
decisions.reason: Chesed is faithful kindness (verse 12); emet is truth, reliability. Together they describe God's love that can be relied on (32:11; Exodus 34:6). The slave's prayer for chesed has been answered.

decisions.choice: as for me, on the way, the LORD led me
decisions.reason: The word order puts "I" first: the slave marvels that he himself, just travelling along, was led by God to the right house.

decisions.choice: my master's brothers: his kinsmen
decisions.reason: "Brothers" (achim) is used broadly for relatives (13:8; 14:14).

decisions.choice: his, he (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: Pronouns for God take the deity pronoun setting.

records.source: וַתָּ֨רָץ֙ הַֽנַּעֲרָ֔ וַתַּגֵּ֖ד לְבֵ֣ית אִמָּ֑הּ כַּדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: And ran the young woman and told [the] household of her mother according to these things.
pieces: The girl ran home and told her mother's household everything that had happened.

L.28: And the young woman ran and told her mother's household about these things.

R.28: Rebekah ran home and told her mother and the others in the house what had happened.

decisions.choice: her mother's household: the women's part of the family
decisions.reason: A daughter would go to the women's quarters or her mother's tent (compare Ruth 1:8; Song of Songs 3:4). It may also hint that her father Bethuel plays little part; her brother Laban takes the lead.

records.source: וּלְרִבְקָ֥ה אָ֖ח וּשְׁמ֣וֹ לָבָ֑ן וַיָּ֨רָץ לָבָ֧ן אֶל־הָאִ֛ישׁ הַח֖וּצָה אֶל־הָעָֽיִן׃
records.gloss: And to Rebekah [was] a brother, and his name [was] Laban; and ran Laban to the man outside to the spring.
pieces: Rebekah's brother, whose name was Laban, ran out to the spring to meet the man.

L.29: Now Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban. And Laban ran out to the man at the spring.

R.29: Rebekah had a brother named Laban. He ran out to the man at the spring.

decisions.choice: Laban: "white"
decisions.reason: The name means "white". Laban's later dealings with Jacob (chapters 29-31) show a shrewd, grasping man; the next verse hints at it already.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י׀כִּרְאֹ֣ת אֶת־הַנֶּ֗זֶם וְֽאֶת־הַצְּמִדִים֮ עַל־יְדֵ֣י אֲחֹתוֹ֒ וּכְשָׁמְע֗וֹ אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֞י רִבְקָ֤ה אֲחֹתוֹ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּֽה־דִבֶּ֥ר אֵלַ֖י הָאִ֑ישׁ וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל־הָאִ֔ישׁ וְהִנֵּ֛ה עֹמֵ֥ד עַל־הַגְּמַלִּ֖ים עַל־הָעָֽיִן׃
records.gloss: And it was, as [he] saw the ring and the bracelets on [the] hands of his sister, and as he heard [the] words of Rebekah his sister, saying, thus spoke to me the man, and he came to the man, and there, he [was] standing by the camels at the spring.
pieces: He had seen the nose ring and the bracelets his sister was wearing, and heard her tell what the man had said to her. So out he went, and there was the man, still standing with the camels by the spring.

L.30: And when he saw the ring, and the bracelets on his sister's arms, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, "This is what the man said to me," he went to the man; and there he was, standing by the camels at the spring.

R.30: Laban had seen the ring and the bracelets on his sister's arms. He had heard her tell what the man said to her. So he went out and found the man standing by his camels near the spring.

decisions.choice: when he saw the ring and the bracelets
decisions.reason: The narrator mentions the gold before the words. Laban's welcome may owe something to the wealth he sees, a first hint of the man Jacob will meet (29:15-27; 31:7).

records.source: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בּ֖וֹא בְּר֣וּךְ יְהוָ֑ה לָ֤מָּה תַעֲמֹד֙ בַּח֔וּץ וְאָנֹכִי֙ פִּנִּ֣יתִי הַבַּ֔יִת וּמָק֖וֹם לַגְּמַלִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And he said, come, blessed of YHWH; why are you standing outside? And I have prepared the house and a place for the camels.
pieces: "Come in, blessed of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!" he said. "Why stay out here? The house is ready for you, and I have made room for the camels."

L.31: And he said, "Come in, you who are blessed by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Why do you stand outside? I have made the house ready, and a place for the camels."

R.31: Laban said, "Come in! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed you. Why are you standing out here? I have a room ready for you in the house, and a place for your camels."

decisions.choice: blessed by the LORD: Laban speaks the divine name
decisions.reason: Laban uses the name of the LORD, having heard the slave's words (verse 27). Laban's family knew of the God of Abraham, though they also kept household gods (31:19, 30).

decisions.choice: I have prepared: cleared and made ready
decisions.reason: The verb (panah, intensive) means to clear away, to make room.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֤א הָאִישׁ֙ הַבַּ֔יְתָה וַיְפַתַּ֖ח הַגְּמַלִּ֑ים וַיִּתֵּ֨ן תֶּ֤בֶן וּמִסְפּוֹא֙ לַגְּמַלִּ֔ים וּמַ֨יִם֙ לִרְחֹ֣ץ רַגְלָ֔יו וְרַגְלֵ֥י הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And came the man into the house, and he unloaded the camels and gave straw and fodder to the camels, and water to wash his feet and [the] feet of the men who [were] with him.
pieces: So the man went into the house. Laban unloaded the camels and gave them straw and feed, and brought water for him and the men with him to wash their feet.

L.32: So the man came into the house, and [Laban] unloaded the camels and gave straw and fodder to the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.

R.32: So the man went into the house. Laban took the loads off the camels and gave them straw and food. He also gave water to the man and the men with him so they could wash their feet.

decisions.choice: he unloaded the camels: Laban, the host
alternatives: the slave unloaded his own camels
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not repeat the subject. The one who gives straw and water for washing is the host, so Laban is meant.

decisions.choice: water to wash his feet
decisions.reason: Washing a guest's feet after a dusty journey was the first act of hospitality (18:4; 19:2). We learn here that the slave did not come alone.

decisions.choice: [Laban] (L); Laban (B, R)
decisions.reason: The subject is supplied so the reader knows who unloaded the camels (m1).

records.source: וַיּוּשַׂ֤ם לְפָנָיו֙ לֶאֱכֹ֔ל וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אֹכַ֔ל עַ֥ד אִם־דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי דְּבָרָ֑י וַיֹּ֖אמֶר דַּבֵּֽר׃
records.gloss: And was set before him to eat; and he said, I will not eat until I have spoken my words. And he said, speak.
pieces: A meal was set before him, but he said, "I will not eat before I have stated my errand." "Go ahead," said Laban.

L.33: And food was set before him to eat, but he said, "I will not eat until I have said what I have to say." And he said, "Speak."

R.33: Then they gave him food. But he said, "I will not eat until I tell you why I came." Laban said, "Go ahead and tell us."

decisions.choice: food was set: the written and the read forms
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text give an active verb, "he (or they) set"; the Masoretes' marginal reading, followed here, gives the passive "was set". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: I will not eat until I have spoken
decisions.reason: Sharing a meal created a bond with a host. The slave puts his master's business first, before he accepts anything from them.

decisions.choice: Laban
decisions.reason: Laban has been the spokesman of the household (verse 31); Balanced and Readable name him.

records.source: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר עֶ֥בֶד אַבְרָהָ֖ם אָנֹֽכִי׃
records.gloss: And he said, [the] servant of Abraham I [am].
pieces: "I am a servant of Abraham," he began.

L.34: And he said, "I am Abraham's slave.

decisions.choice: Abraham's slave I am: the speaker introduces himself by his master
decisions.reason: He gives no name of his own. The whole speech that follows (verses 34-49) is about his master and his master's God.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַיהוָ֞ה בֵּרַ֧ךְ אֶת־אֲדֹנִ֛י מְאֹ֖ד וַיִּגְדָּ֑ל וַיִּתֶּן־ל֞וֹ צֹ֤אן וּבָקָר֙ וְכֶ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֔ב וַעֲבָדִם֙ וּשְׁפָחֹ֔ת וּגְמַלִּ֖ים וַחֲמֹרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And YHWH has blessed my master exceedingly, and he has become great; and he has given him sheep and cattle and silver and gold and male servants and female servants and camels and donkeys.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has greatly blessed my master, and he has become a rich and powerful man. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, servants both male and female, camels and donkeys.

L.35: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed my master greatly, and he has become great. He has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, male and female slaves, camels and donkeys.

R.35: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed my master very much, and he has become very rich. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has given him sheep, goats and cattle, silver and gold, men and women servants, and camels and donkeys.

decisions.choice: the LORD has blessed my master: wealth as God's gift
decisions.reason: The slave tells the story so that the family sees God's hand in all of it. He begins with what the narrator said in verse 1: the LORD has blessed Abraham.

decisions.choice: the LORD has given him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat the divine name so that it is clear the giver is the LORD, not Abraham.

decisions.choice: male and female servants
decisions.reason: "Male and female servants" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; Literal keeps "male and female slaves".

records.source: וַתֵּ֡לֶד שָׂרָה֩ אֵ֨שֶׁת אֲדֹנִ֥י בֵן֙ לַֽאדֹנִ֔י אַחֲרֵ֖י זִקְנָתָ֑הּ וַיִּתֶּן־לּ֖וֹאֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And bore Sarah, [the] wife of my master, a son to my master after her old age; and he has given to him all that [is] to him.
pieces: Sarah, my master's wife, gave him a son when she was already old, and my master has handed over to him everything he owns.

L.36: And Sarah my master's wife bore a son to my master when she was old, and he has given him all that he has.

R.36: Sarah, my master's wife, gave birth to his son when she was very old. That son will have everything my master owns.

decisions.choice: after her old age: born when Sarah was past childbearing
decisions.reason: Sarah bore Isaac at ninety (17:17; 21:2). The slave tells the family that the son is a child of God's promise.

decisions.choice: he has given him all that he has: Isaac is sole heir
decisions.reason: Isaac will inherit everything (compare 25:5). For the bride's family this means she will marry the heir of a great estate.

records.source: וַיַּשְׁבִּעֵ֥נִי אֲדֹנִ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹא־תִקַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ לִבְנִ֔י מִבְּנוֹת֙ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י יֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּאַרְצֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And made me swear my master, saying, you will not take a wife for my son from [the] daughters of the Canaanite[s] in whose land I [am] dwelling,
pieces: My master put me under oath: 'You are not to find a wife for my son among the women of the Canaanites, whose land I live in.

L.37: And my master made me swear, saying, 'You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I dwell,

R.37: My master made me promise him with an oath. He said, 'Do not choose a wife for my son from the Canaanite women who live in this land.

records.source: אִם־לֹ֧א אֶל־בֵּית־אָבִ֛י תֵּלֵ֖ךְ וְאֶל־מִשְׁפַּחְתִּ֑י וְלָקַחְתָּ֥ אִשָּׁ֖ה לִבְנִֽי׃
records.gloss: but to [the] house of my father you will go and to my family, and you will take a wife for my son.
pieces: No, you must travel to my father's house, to my own kin, and bring back a wife for my son from there.'

L.38: but you shall go to my father's house and to my family, and take a wife for my son.'

R.38: Instead, go to my father's family, to my own relatives, and find a wife for my son there.'

decisions.choice: but to my father's house: a strong oath form
decisions.reason: The words "if not" ('im lo') here mean "you shall surely", the form of an oath. In retelling the charge the slave speaks of Abraham's "father's house" and "family", stressing the family tie for his hearers (Abraham said "my land and my kindred", verse 4).

records.source: וָאֹמַ֖ר אֶל־אֲדֹנִ֑י אֻלַ֛י לֹא־תֵלֵ֥ךְ הָאִשָּׁ֖ה אַחֲרָֽי׃
records.gloss: And I said to my master, perhaps not will go the woman after me.
pieces: 'But suppose the woman will not follow me?' I asked my master.

L.39: And I said to my master, 'Perhaps the woman will not follow me.'

R.39: I said to my master, 'The woman might not want to come with me.'

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י יְהוָ֞ה אֲשֶׁר־הִתְהַלַּ֣כְתִּי לְפָנָ֗יו יִשְׁלַ֨ח מַלְאָכ֤וֹ אִתָּךְ֙ וְהִצְלִ֣יחַ דַּרְכֶּ֔ךָ וְלָקַחְתָּ֤ אִשָּׁה֙ לִבְנִ֔י מִמִּשְׁפַּחְתִּ֖י וּמִבֵּ֥ית אָבִֽי׃
records.gloss: And he said to me, YHWH, before whom I have walked, he will send his angel with you and will make successful your journey, and you will take a wife for my son from my family and from [the] house of my father.
pieces: He answered, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, in whose presence I have lived my life, will send {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angel with you and give your journey success. You will get a wife for my son from my clan, from my father's family.

L.40: And he said to me, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, before whom I have walked, will send {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angel with you and make your journey successful, and you shall take a wife for my son from my family and from my father's house.

R.40: He answered, 'I have always lived to please {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will send {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angel with you and will make your trip a success. You will find a wife for my son from my relatives, from my father's family.

decisions.choice: before whom I have walked: lived in his presence, serving him
decisions.reason: To walk before God is to live one's life in his sight, faithful to him. God had told Abraham, "Walk before me and be blameless" (17:1).

decisions.choice: his (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: "His" refers to the LORD and takes the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: I have always lived to please the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means (m1).

records.source: אָ֤ז תִּנָּקֶה֙ מֵאָ֣לָתִ֔י כִּ֥י תָב֖וֹא אֶל־מִשְׁפַּחְתִּ֑י וְאִם־לֹ֤א יִתְּנוּ֙ לָ֔ךְ וְהָיִ֥יתָ נָקִ֖י מֵאָלָתִֽי׃
records.gloss: Then you will be free from my oath, when you go to my family; and if they do not give [her] to you, then you will be free from my oath.
pieces: You will be free of the oath you swore me once you have gone to my family. Even if they refuse to give her to you, you will be free of it.'

L.41: Then you will be free from my curse, when you come to my family; and if they will not give [her] to you, you will be free from my curse.'

R.41: If you go to my relatives and they will not let her go with you, then you do not have to keep your promise to me.'

decisions.choice: my curse ('alah): the curse that seals an oath
decisions.reason: In verse 8 Abraham used the ordinary word for oath (shevu'ah); here the slave uses 'alah, the curse that falls on one who breaks an oath. The meaning is the same: he will be released.

decisions.choice: curse (L); oath (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal shows the different word (m1); Balanced and Readable keep the plain sense, the oath.

records.gloss: And I came today to the spring and said, YHWH, God of my master Abraham, if you, please, are making successful my journey on which I am going,
pieces: Today, when I reached the spring, I prayed: '{{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, God of my master Abraham, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} mean to prosper the errand I have come on,

L.42: And I came today to the spring and said, '{{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, God of my master Abraham, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will now make successful the journey on which I am going,

R.42: Today, when I came to the spring, I prayed, '{{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, God of my master Abraham, please make my trip a success.

decisions.choice: you, your (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: The slave speaks to God, so "you" and "your" take the deity pronoun setting.

records.source: הִנֵּ֛ה אָנֹכִ֥י נִצָּ֖ב עַל־עֵ֣ין הַמָּ֑יִם וְהָיָ֤ה הָֽעַלְמָה֙ הַיֹּצֵ֣את לִשְׁאֹ֔ב וְאָמַרְתִּ֣י אֵלֶ֔יהָ הַשְׁקִֽינִי־נָ֥א מְעַט־מַ֖יִם מִכַּדֵּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: here, I [am] standing by [the] spring of water; and let it be [that] the young woman who comes out to draw water, and I say to her, give me to drink, please, a little water from your jar,
pieces: here I stand at the spring. Let it be like this: a young woman comes out for water, and I ask her, "Will you give me a little water from your jar to drink?"

L.43: look, I am standing by the spring of water. Let it be that the young woman who comes out to draw water, to whom I say, "Please give me a little water from your jar to drink,"

R.43: I am standing here by the spring. When a young woman comes to get water, I will say to her, "Please give me a little water from your jar."

decisions.choice: young woman ('almah): a girl of marriageable age
decisions.reason: Here the slave uses 'almah, a young woman old enough to marry, in place of na'arah (verse 14). Of Rebekah both words fit, and verse 16 has already said she was a virgin. The same word is used in Isaiah 7:14.

records.source: וְאָמְרָ֤ה אֵלַי֙ גַּם־אַתָּ֣ה שְׁתֵ֔ה וְגַ֥ם לִגְמַלֶּ֖יךָ אֶשְׁאָ֑ב הִ֣וא הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־הֹכִ֥יחַ יְהוָ֖ה לְבֶן־אֲדֹנִֽי׃
records.gloss: and she says to me, both you drink and also for your camels I will draw water, she [is] the woman whom has appointed YHWH for [the] son of my master.
pieces: and she answers, "Drink, and I will fetch water for your camels too." May she be the woman {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has marked out for my master's son.'

L.44: and who says to me, "Drink, and I will draw for your camels too," let her be the woman whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has appointed for my master's son.'

R.44: If she says, "Drink, and I will get water for your camels too," then let her be the woman {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has chosen for my master's son.'

records.source: אֲנִי֩ טֶ֨רֶם אֲכַלֶּ֜ה לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל־לִבִּ֗י וְהִנֵּ֨ה רִבְקָ֤ה יֹצֵאת֙ וְכַדָּ֣הּ עַל־שִׁכְמָ֔הּ וַתֵּ֥רֶד הָעַ֖יְנָה וַתִּשְׁאָ֑ב וָאֹמַ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יהָ הַשְׁקִ֥ינִי נָֽא׃
records.gloss: I, not yet had I finished speaking to my heart, and there, Rebekah [was] coming out, and her jar [was] on her shoulder; and she went down to the spring and drew water. And I said to her, give me a drink, please.
pieces: Before my silent prayer was finished, out came Rebekah, her jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and drew water, and I asked her, 'Please give me a drink.'

L.45: Before I had finished speaking in my heart, look, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder, and she went down to the spring and drew water. And I said to her, 'Please give me a drink.'

R.45: I was still praying silently when Rebekah came with her jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and filled it. I said to her, 'Please give me a drink.'

decisions.choice: speaking to my heart: praying silently
decisions.reason: To speak "to one's heart" is to speak inwardly, to oneself (8:21; 27:41). The slave's prayer was silent; no one but God could have known it.

records.source: וַתְּמַהֵ֗ר וַתּ֤וֹרֶד כַּדָּהּ֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יהָ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁתֵ֔ה וְגַם־גְּמַלֶּ֖יךָ אַשְׁקֶ֑ה וָאֵ֕שְׁתְּ וְגַ֥ם הַגְּמַלִּ֖ים הִשְׁקָֽתָה׃
records.gloss: And she hurried and lowered her jar from upon her and said, drink, and also your camels I will give drink. And I drank, and also the camels she gave drink.
pieces: At once she lowered the jar from her shoulder. 'Drink,' she said, 'and I will give your camels water as well.' I drank, and she gave water to the camels too.

L.46: And she quickly lowered her jar from her shoulder and said, 'Drink, and I will water your camels too.' So I drank, and she watered the camels too.

R.46: Right away she lowered her jar. She said, 'Drink, and I will give your camels water too.' So I drank, and she gave the camels water as well.

records.source: וָאֶשְׁאַ֣ל אֹתָ֗הּ וָאֹמַר֮ בַּת־מִ֣י אַתְּ֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר בַּת־בְּתוּאֵל֙ בֶּן־נָח֔וֹר אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָֽלְדָה־לּ֖וֹ מִלְכָּ֑ה וָאָשִׂ֤ם הַנֶּ֨זֶם֙ עַל־אַפָּ֔הּ וְהַצְּמִידִ֖ים עַל־יָדֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And I asked her and said, daughter of whom [are] you? And she said, [the] daughter of Bethuel, son of Nahor, whom bore to him Milcah. And I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her hands.
pieces: I asked her whose daughter she was, and she told me, 'Bethuel's, the son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore to him.' So I fitted the ring to her nose and put the bracelets on her arms.

L.47: Then I asked her, 'Whose daughter are you?' And she said, 'The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor's son, whom Milcah bore to him.' So I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her arms.

R.47: I asked her, 'Who is your father?' She said, 'My father is Bethuel. His parents are Nahor and Milcah.' So I put the ring in her nose and the bracelets on her arms.

decisions.choice: first the question, then the gifts: a careful retelling
decisions.reason: In verses 22-23 the slave brought out the gifts before he asked her name. Telling it to her family, he puts the question first, so that the gifts appear as a response to learning she was kin. The retelling also leaves out the camels kneeling and his gazing in silence, and stresses God's leading.

records.source: וָאֶקֹּ֥ד וָֽאֶשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֖ה לַיהוָ֑ה וָאֲבָרֵ֗ךְ אֶת־יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י אַבְרָהָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִנְחַ֨נִי֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ אֱמֶ֔ת לָקַ֛חַת אֶת־בַּת־אֲחִ֥י אֲדֹנִ֖י לִבְנֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And I bowed and bowed down to YHWH, and I blessed YHWH, [the] God of my master Abraham, who had led me in [the] way of truth to take [the] daughter of [the] brother of my master for his son.
pieces: Then I knelt and worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I blessed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of my master Abraham, for guiding me along the true road, to take my master's kinswoman, his brother's granddaughter, as a wife for his son.

L.48: And I bowed my head and worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I blessed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me by the right way to take the daughter of my master's brother for his son.

R.48: I bowed down and worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I thanked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of my master Abraham. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had led me straight to the family of my master's brother to find a wife for his son.

decisions.choice: the way of truth: the right road, the true way
decisions.reason: "Truth" ('emet) here means reliable, right: God led him by the road that brought him exactly where he needed to be.

decisions.choice: the daughter of my master's brother: his kinswoman
decisions.reason: Rebekah is the granddaughter of Abraham's brother Nahor (verse 24). "Daughter" and "brother" are used broadly for descendants and relatives.

decisions.choice: granddaughter
decisions.reason: Balanced states the exact relationship (m2); Literal keeps "daughter".

records.source: וְ֠עַתָּה אִם־יֶשְׁכֶ֨ם עֹשִׂ֜ים חֶ֧סֶד וֶֽאֱמֶ֛ת אֶת־אֲדֹנִ֖י הַגִּ֣ידוּ לִ֑י וְאִם־לֹ֕א הַגִּ֣ידוּ לִ֔י וְאֶפְנֶ֥ה עַל־יָמִ֖ין א֥וֹ עַל־שְׂמֹֽאל׃
records.gloss: And now, if you are doing loyalty and faithfulness with my master, tell me; and if not, tell me, that I may turn to [the] right or to [the] left.
pieces: Now then, if you are willing to act in faithful kindness toward my master, tell me. If not, say so, and I will turn elsewhere, to the right hand or the left."

L.49: And now, if you will deal loyally and faithfully with my master, tell me; and if not, tell me, so that I may turn to the right or to the left."

R.49: Now, please tell me if you will be kind and loyal to my master and let Rebekah come. If not, tell me, so that I can decide what to do next."

decisions.choice: loyalty and faithfulness: the words used of God in verse 27
decisions.reason: The slave asks the family to show Abraham the same chesed and 'emet that God has shown him (verse 27): to keep faith with their kinsman by giving Rebekah.

decisions.choice: turn to the right or to the left: know what to do next
decisions.reason: The phrase means to go another way, to look elsewhere. The slave asks for a plain answer.

decisions.choice: and let Rebekah come
decisions.reason: Readable says what the family's loyalty would mean in practice.

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַן לָבָ֤ן וּבְתוּאֵל֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מֵיְהוָ֖ה יָצָ֣א הַדָּבָ֑ר לֹ֥א נוּכַ֛ל דַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ רַ֥ע אוֹ־טֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: And answered Laban and Bethuel and said, from YHWH has come out the matter; we are not able to speak to you bad or good.
pieces: Laban and Bethuel replied, "This has come from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It is not for us to say anything for it or against it.

L.50: Then Laban and Bethuel answered and said, "The matter comes from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; we cannot say anything to you, bad or good.

R.50: Laban and Bethuel answered, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has done this. We cannot say yes or no.

decisions.choice: Laban and Bethuel: brother and father
decisions.reason: Rebekah's father Bethuel is named only here; elsewhere her brother Laban and her mother act for the family (verses 53, 55). A brother often had a large say in his sister's marriage (compare 34:11-13).

decisions.choice: we cannot speak bad or good: we have nothing to say
decisions.reason: "Bad or good" means anything at all (31:24, 29). Since the LORD has plainly decided, the family can add nothing and will not object.

records.source: הִנֵּֽה־רִבְקָ֥ה לְפָנֶ֖יךָ קַ֣ח וָלֵ֑ךְ וּתְהִ֤י אִשָּׁה֙ לְבֶן־אֲדֹנֶ֔יךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Here, Rebekah [is] before you; take [her] and go, and let her be a wife for [the] son of your master, as has spoken YHWH.
pieces: Rebekah is here in front of you. Take her with you and go; she shall be your master's son's wife, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has declared."

L.51: Look, Rebekah is before you; take [her] and go, and let her be the wife of your master's son, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken."

R.51: Rebekah is right here. Take her with you. She will marry your master's son, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said."

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֛ע עֶ֥בֶד אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֶת־דִּבְרֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ אַ֖רְצָה לַֽיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was, when heard [the] servant of Abraham their words, and he bowed down to the ground to YHWH.
pieces: At their answer, Abraham's servant bowed low to the ground before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.52: And when Abraham's slave heard their words, he bowed himself to the ground before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.52: When Abraham's servant heard this, he bowed down to the ground and worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: he bowed to the ground before the LORD
decisions.reason: For the third time the slave turns to God (verses 26, 48). Before he thanks the family, he thanks the LORD.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַיּוֹצֵ֨א הָעֶ֜בֶד כְּלֵי־כֶ֨סֶף וּכְלֵ֤י זָהָב֙ וּבְגָדִ֔ים וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לְרִבְקָ֑ה וּמִ֨גְדָּנֹ֔ת נָתַ֥ן לְאָחִ֖יהָ וּלְאִמָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And brought out the servant articles of silver and articles of gold and garments and gave [them] to Rebekah; and costly gifts he gave to her brother and to her mother.
pieces: Next the servant brought out silver and gold ornaments and garments as gifts for Rebekah, and he presented rich gifts to her brother and her mother as well.

L.53: And the slave brought out articles of silver and articles of gold, and garments, and gave [them] to Rebekah; he also gave costly gifts to her brother and to her mother.

R.53: Then the servant brought out jewelry made of silver and gold, and clothes, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave expensive gifts to her brother and her mother.

decisions.choice: silver, gold and garments: gifts for the bride
decisions.reason: The word kelim covers objects of many kinds: jewelry, vessels, ornaments. Gifts to the bride and her family sealed a marriage agreement; Israel later knew a fixed bride-price (mohar, 34:12; Exodus 22:16).

decisions.choice: costly gifts (migdanot): choice things
decisions.reason: The word means precious, choice things (Deuteronomy 33:13-16 uses a related word of the best gifts of nature).

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַיֹּאכְל֣וּ וַיִּשְׁתּ֗וּ ה֛וּא וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־עִמּ֖וֹ וַיָּלִ֑ינוּ וַיָּק֣וּמוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שַׁלְּחֻ֥נִי לַֽאדֹנִֽי׃
records.gloss: And they ate and drank, he and the men who [were] with him, and they lodged. And they arose in the morning, and he said, send me away to my master.
pieces: Only then did he and his companions eat and drink, and they stayed overnight. In the morning, when they were up, he said, "Let me return to my master."

L.54: And they ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and spent the night. When they rose in the morning, he said, "Send me away to my master."

R.54: Then he and his men ate and drank, and they stayed there that night. When they got up the next morning, the servant said, "Let me go back to my master now."

decisions.choice: they ate and drank: the meal that seals the agreement
decisions.reason: The slave would not eat before his errand was told (verse 33). Now the meal marks the agreement as settled.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker, Abraham's servant ("servant" in Readable, as the style guide has it); the Hebrew has only "he said".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אָחִ֨יהָ֙ וְאִמָּ֔הּ תֵּשֵׁ֨ב הַנַּעֲרָ֥ אִתָּ֛נוּ יָמִ֖ים א֣וֹ עָשׂ֑וֹר אַחַ֖ר תֵּלֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And said her brother and her mother, let remain the young woman with us days or ten; after she will go.
pieces: Her brother and mother, though, wanted a delay: "Let the girl stay with us some days, perhaps ten. After that she may go."

L.55: And her brother and her mother said, "Let the young woman stay with us some days, or ten; after that she may go."

R.55: But her brother and her mother said, "Let Rebekah stay with us a little while, about ten days. Then she can go."

decisions.choice: days or ten: a while, perhaps ten days
decisions.reason: "Days" can mean a set period, sometimes a year (Leviticus 25:29); some take the phrase as "a year or ten months". More likely it means "a few days, say ten". Either way, they want to delay the parting.

decisions.choice: her brother and her mother speak
decisions.reason: Bethuel, named in verse 50, is not mentioned again. Laban and his mother act for the family, as at the start (verses 28-29).

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ אַל־תְּאַחֲר֣וּ אֹתִ֔י וַֽיהוָ֖ה הִצְלִ֣יחַ דַּרְכִּ֑י שַׁלְּח֕וּנִי וְאֵלְכָ֖ה לַֽאדֹנִֽי׃
records.gloss: And he said to them, do not delay me, and YHWH has made successful my journey; send me away, that I may go to my master.
pieces: "Do not keep me waiting," he said, "since {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has made my journey succeed. Let me leave and go back to my master."

L.56: And he said to them, "Do not delay me, since {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has made my journey successful. Send me away, so that I may go to my master."

R.56: He said to them, "Please do not keep me here. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has made my trip a success. Let me go back to my master."

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ נִקְרָ֣א לַֽנַּעֲרָ֑ וְנִשְׁאֲלָ֖ה אֶת־פִּֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And they said, let us call the young woman and ask her mouth.
pieces: "Let us call the girl," they said, "and hear what she says."

L.57: And they said, "Let us call the young woman and ask her own mouth."

R.57: They said, "Let us call Rebekah and ask her what she wants."

decisions.choice: ask her mouth: ask her directly
decisions.reason: To "ask someone's mouth" is to hear the answer from the person herself. The marriage was already agreed (verse 51); the question is whether she will leave at once.

records.source: וַיִּקְרְא֤וּ לְרִבְקָה֙ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יהָ הֲתֵלְכִ֖י עִם־הָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֑ה וַתֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And they called Rebekah and said to her, will you go with this man? And she said, I will go.
pieces: They called Rebekah in. "Are you willing to go now with this man?" they asked. "I will go," she answered.

L.58: And they called Rebekah and said to her, "Will you go with this man?" And she said, "I will go."

R.58: They called Rebekah and asked her, "Do you want to go with this man now?" She said, "Yes, I will go."

decisions.choice: I will go: Rebekah's answer echoes Abraham's journey
decisions.reason: In one Hebrew word ('elekh) Rebekah agrees to leave her family and her land for a land she has never seen, as Abraham did when God called him (12:1, 4: "go" ... "and Abram went").

decisions.choice: now
decisions.reason: The question is about leaving at once, not about the marriage, which was already agreed (verses 51, 55).

records.source: וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֛וּ אֶת־רִבְקָ֥ה אֲחֹתָ֖ם וְאֶת־מֵנִקְתָּ֑הּ וְאֶת־עֶ֥בֶד אַבְרָהָ֖ם וְאֶת־אֲנָשָֽׁיו׃
records.gloss: And they sent away Rebekah their sister and her nurse and [the] servant of Abraham and his men.
pieces: So they said goodbye to their sister Rebekah and her nurse, and sent them off with Abraham's servant and his men.

L.59: So they sent away Rebekah their sister and her nurse, and Abraham's slave and his men.

R.59: Rebekah's family let her leave with her nurse. Abraham's servant and his men went with them.

decisions.choice: her nurse: the woman who had cared for her from childhood
decisions.reason: Her nurse is later named Deborah; she lived with Jacob's household until her death (35:8). A nurse often stayed with a girl of a wealthy family for life.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַיְבָרֲכ֤וּ אֶת־רִבְקָה֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ לָ֔הּ אֲחֹתֵ֕נוּ אַ֥תְּ הֲיִ֖י לְאַלְפֵ֣י רְבָבָ֑ה וְיִירַ֣שׁ זַרְעֵ֔ךְ אֵ֖ת שַׁ֥עַר שֹׂנְאָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And they blessed Rebekah and said to her, our sister, you, become thousands of ten thousand; and may possess your offspring [the] gate of [those] hating it.
pieces: They gave Rebekah their blessing: "Sister, may you become the mother of countless thousands. May your descendants take the cities of their enemies."

L.60: And they blessed Rebekah and said to her, "Our sister, may you become thousands of ten thousands, and may your offspring possess the gate of those who hate them."

R.60: They blessed Rebekah and said, "Sister, may you become the mother of millions of people. May your descendants defeat their enemies and take over their cities."

decisions.choice: thousands of ten thousands: countless descendants
decisions.reason: Ten thousand (revavah) was the largest number in common use; "thousands of ten thousands" means more than can be counted.

decisions.choice: possess the gate of their enemies: the words of 22:17
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham the same, "your offspring shall possess the gate of his enemies" (22:17). To hold a city's gate was to control the city. Unknowingly, Rebekah's family blesses her with the blessing of the promise.

decisions.choice: millions of people
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the number (m1).

records.source: וַתָּ֨קָם רִבְקָ֜ה וְנַעֲרֹתֶ֗יהָ וַתִּרְכַּ֨בְנָה֙ עַל־הַגְּמַלִּ֔ים וַתֵּלַ֖כְנָה אַחֲרֵ֣י הָאִ֑ישׁ וַיִּקַּ֥ח הָעֶ֛בֶד אֶת־רִבְקָ֖ה וַיֵּלַֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And arose Rebekah and her young women, and they rode on the camels and went after the man; and took the servant Rebekah and went.
pieces: Rebekah and her young women set out, riding on the camels behind the man. So the servant took Rebekah and began the journey home.

L.61: And Rebekah and her young women arose, and they rode on the camels and followed the man. So the slave took Rebekah and went.

R.61: Rebekah and the young women who served her got on the camels and followed the man. So the servant took Rebekah and started for home.

decisions.choice: her young women: attendants
decisions.reason: The word (na'arot) means young women, here those who attended Rebekah, as in Exodus 2:5 and Esther 4:4. She leaves as the daughter of a wealthy house.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וְיִצְחָק֙ בָּ֣א מִבּ֔וֹא בְּאֵ֥ר לַחַ֖י רֹאִ֑י וְה֥וּא יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּאֶ֥רֶץ הַנֶּֽגֶב׃
records.gloss: And Isaac had come from coming [to] Beer-lahai-roi, and he [was] dwelling in [the] land of the Negev.
pieces: Meanwhile Isaac had come back from Beer-lahai-roi; he was living in the Negev at the time.

L.62: Now Isaac had come from going to Beer-lahai-roi, for he was dwelling in the land of the Negev.

R.62: Meanwhile Isaac had come back from a well called Beer-lahai-roi. He was living in the Negev, the dry land in the south.

decisions.choice: had come from going to Beer-lahai-roi: an unusual phrase
alternatives: had come through the wilderness to Beer-lahai-roi
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "came from coming" is awkward. The Septuagint reads "was going through the wilderness to", and the Samaritan Pentateuch has "came into the wilderness of". The Hebrew text is followed: Isaac had returned from the well where God once saw Hagar (16:14) and where he later lived (25:11).

decisions.choice: the Negev: the dry south country
decisions.reason: The Negev is the dry region south of Hebron, where Abraham lived at times (20:1).

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֥א יִצְחָ֛ק לָשׂ֥וּחַ בַּשָּׂדֶ֖ה לִפְנ֣וֹת עָ֑רֶב וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּ֥ה גְמַלִּ֖ים בָּאִֽים׃
records.gloss: And went out Isaac to meditate in the field at [the] turning of evening, and he lifted up his eyes and saw, and there, camels [were] coming.
pieces: Toward evening Isaac had gone out into the countryside to reflect, and raising his eyes he saw camels on their way.

L.63: And Isaac went out to meditate in the field toward evening; and he lifted up his eyes and saw, and look, camels were coming.

R.63: One evening Isaac went out into the field to think and pray. When he looked up, he saw camels coming.

decisions.choice: to meditate (lasuach): meaning uncertain
decisions.reason: The verb occurs only here. It may be related to words for musing, complaint or prayer (Psalm 55:18 uses a similar word), or mean simply to stroll. Isaac may have been grieving his mother (verse 67).

decisions.choice: at the turning of evening: as evening came
decisions.reason: The phrase means the time when day turns toward evening. The slave first met Rebekah at evening too (verse 11).

decisions.choice: to think and pray
decisions.reason: Readable gives two of the likely senses (m1).

records.source: וַתִּשָּׂ֤א רִבְקָה֙ אֶת־עֵינֶ֔יהָ וַתֵּ֖רֶא אֶת־יִצְחָ֑ק וַתִּפֹּ֖ל מֵעַ֥ל הַגָּמָֽל׃
records.gloss: And lifted up Rebekah her eyes and saw Isaac, and she fell from upon the camel.
pieces: Rebekah, for her part, raised her eyes, and at the sight of Isaac she got down quickly from the camel.

L.64: And Rebekah lifted up her eyes and saw Isaac, and she dismounted from the camel.

R.64: When Rebekah looked up and saw Isaac, she slid down quickly from her camel.

decisions.choice: she fell from the camel: she got down quickly
decisions.reason: The verb "fall" (naphal) here means a quick dismount (compare 2 Kings 5:21). To get down was a mark of respect to someone approaching.

records.source: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־הָעֶ֗בֶד מִֽי־הָאִ֤ישׁ הַלָּזֶה֙ הַהֹלֵ֤ךְ בַּשָּׂדֶה֙ לִקְרָאתֵ֔נוּ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הָעֶ֖בֶד ה֣וּא אֲדֹנִ֑י וַתִּקַּ֥ח הַצָּעִ֖יף וַתִּתְכָּֽס׃
records.gloss: And she said to the servant, who [is] that man, the [one] walking in the field to meet us? And said the servant, he [is] my master. And she took the veil and covered herself.
pieces: "Who is that man walking through the field toward us?" she asked the servant. "It is my master," he replied. So she drew her veil over her face.

L.65: And she said to the slave, "Who is that man walking in the field to meet us?" And the slave said, "He is my master." So she took her veil and covered herself.

R.65: She asked the servant, "Who is that man walking across the field to meet us?" The servant answered, "That is my master." So Rebekah put on her veil to cover her face.

decisions.choice: my master: now Isaac
decisions.reason: Until now the slave's master was Abraham. Isaac, heir of all his father has (verse 36), is now called "my master"; Abraham is not seen again in the chapter.

decisions.choice: she took her veil and covered herself: the custom of a bride
decisions.reason: A bride was veiled before her bridegroom until the marriage (compare 29:23-25, where the veil hides Leah). Rebekah shows modesty and marks herself as Isaac's bride.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַיְסַפֵּ֥ר הָעֶ֖בֶד לְיִצְחָ֑ק אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃
records.gloss: And recounted the servant to Isaac all the things which he had done.
pieces: The servant reported to Isaac everything he had done.

L.66: And the slave told Isaac all the things that he had done.

R.66: The servant told Isaac everything that had happened.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַיְבִאֶ֣הָ יִצְחָ֗ק הָאֹ֨הֱלָה֙ שָׂרָ֣ה אִמּ֔וֹ וַיִּקַּ֧ח אֶת־רִבְקָ֛ה וַתְּהִי־ל֥וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֖ה וַיֶּאֱהָבֶ֑הָ וַיִּנָּחֵ֥ם יִצְחָ֖ק אַחֲרֵ֥י אִמּֽוֹ׃פ
records.gloss: And brought her Isaac to the tent [of] Sarah his mother, and he took Rebekah and she became to him for a wife, and he loved her; and was comforted Isaac after his mother.
pieces: Isaac brought Rebekah into the tent that had been his mother Sarah's. He took her as his wife, and he loved her. So Isaac was consoled for the loss of his mother.

L.67: And Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother, and he took Rebekah, and she became his wife, and he loved her. So Isaac was comforted after his mother['s death].

R.67: Isaac took Rebekah into the tent where his mother Sarah had lived, and she became his wife. Isaac loved her, and she comforted him after his mother died.

decisions.choice: the tent of Sarah his mother: an unusual phrase
alternatives: into the tent (Sarah his mother omitted)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "into the tent, Sarah his mother", awkward grammar. It is usually taken to mean Sarah's tent, which had stood empty since her death (23:2). Rebekah takes Sarah's place as the mother of the family.

decisions.choice: and he loved her: love within marriage
decisions.reason: This is one of the few places in the Bible that says a husband loved his wife. The love follows the marriage, which God arranged.

decisions.choice: comforted after his mother: three years of grief
decisions.reason: Sarah died at 127 (23:1), when Isaac was thirty-seven (17:17; 21:5); he married at forty (25:20). His grief for his mother is ended by his love for his wife.

decisions.choice: after his mother['s death]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "after his mother"; Literal brackets the word needed.

decisions.choice: she comforted him
decisions.reason: Readable makes Rebekah the one who comforted him, which the verse implies.
